key: Then he saw in that very space a woman beautifully adorned, Uma of golden hue, daughter of Haimavat (Himalaya).
s: The mystery that baffled Agni and Vayu vanishes before Indra, and a figure appears; Śaṅkara, on 3.12, reads the woman as knowledge, taking Uma’s form because Indra, drawn to the Spirit, stayed pondering it where Agni and Vayu turned back.

evidence.words: Indra stood discussing within himself what that Spirit was, and did not return like Agni and Vayu . Seeing his attachment to that Spirit, knowledge in the form of a woman and of Uma appeared before him. Indra beheld knowledge, fairest of the fair,
evidence.lang: English (Sitarama Sastri’s translation of Śaṅkara’s Sanskrit, OCR as printed)
evidence.gloss: Indra stood considering within himself what that Spirit was, and did not go back as Agni and Vāyu had. Seeing his attachment to that Spirit, knowledge appeared before him in the form of a woman, Umā. Indra beheld knowledge, fairest of the fair.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Kena Upanishad 3.12, at [161]; one whole sentence at the head of the unit). Plain sense gives the setting in the day’s own terms: Agni and Vayu fail at 3.6 and 3.10, the mystery vanishes before Indra at 3.11, a figure appears. Śaṅkara comments on 3.11 together with 3.12 (the packet places the comment in the 3.12 segment), and the relevant words gloss 3.12: Indra stood pondering what the Spirit was and did not return like Agni and Vayu; seeing his attachment to the Spirit, knowledge in the form of a woman, Umā, appeared. The reading (woman as knowledge, in Umā’s form, because of Indra’s attachment and staying where the others turned back) is carried without drift; ‘on 3.12’ is an accurate place. Madhva’s Brahma-Sāra story differs (Umā left behind by Brahman as the fit teacher) and is not attributed. entry-check ok, 40 words.
